verified: ULA's own Nov. 17 statement says low booster performance shortly after liftoff caused stage separation below the altitude and velocity needed for orbit, that the Centaur V upper stage and solid rocket boosters performed nominally, and that the mission was lost around 10 minutes into flight; Space.com reports the payload was 40 Amazon Leo satellites.
unconfirmed: the specific fault in the first-stage booster, and whether the BE-4 engines are implicated — that suggestion rests on unnamed sources cited by Ars Technica, and ULA says identifying the problem will take more time. Also unconfirmed: any return-to-flight date or the scope of the investigation.

verified: ULA在11月17日的更新中表示，11月15日的发射在升空后不久出现一级助推器性能不足，级间分离时高度过低、速度不足以入轨，约10分钟后遥测和任务丢失；半人马座V上面级和固体助推器均正常。Space.com报道称，本次搭载的40颗Amazon Leo卫星全部损失。
unconfirmed: 一级故障的具体部件和原因，以及是否涉及BE-4发动机；Ars Technica引述消息人士称初步数据可能不指向BE-4，但ULA未确认，也未给出调查时间表。

titles.en: Vulcan return-to-flight fails; ULA cites low booster performance, cause unknown
titles.zh: ULA证实Vulcan复飞失败，故障是否涉及BE-4仍未知
